Hi Tom / Aanya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on the customer support use case and the ~100k annual ticket volume. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get a customer-specific eval running on Redwood: 

Recap
- Primary goal: measure model accuracy on intent classification + slot extraction for your top 5 ticket types, and track regression risk when we test quantized variants.
- Success criteria you shared: >= 92% intent accuracy, slot extraction F1 >= 0.88, and no more than 3% user-facing downgrade vs current baseline on priority flows.

Recommended baseline models to evaluate (order of preference)
1) Redwood-3.1 (quantized Q5/Q4) — best latency/cost tradeoff for long context; recommended for production trials.
2) Redwood-1-7B (FP16) — faster and cheaper for short-context classification tasks, useful as a low-cost baseline.
3) Open-compat model (Llama 3 family) — for parity checks; we can run to compare hallucination rates.

What we need from you to run a customer-specific eval on Redwood
- A labeled sample dataset (we recommend 2k–5k rows for reliable metrics). Preferred format: JSONL with fields: id, input_text, intent_label, slots (object or list), and tags for priority_flow. See example attached (example_dataset.jsonl).
- A short prompt set for each task (attached: midcity_promptset.csv) — these are the canonical prompts we'll use for scoring.
- Confirmation of scoring criteria (outlined below).

How Redwood will run the eval (high level)- We'll spin up a short-lived eval deployment using your account (private eval workspace). The eval will:
  1) run each model variant against the dataset (streaming batch runner)
  2) capture model outputs, token-level timing, and cost estimates
  3) compute automated metrics (intent accuracy, slot F1, response length distribution, hallucination flags) and surface per-case failures for manual review

Scoring criteria (what we'll compute)
- Intent accuracy (primary)
- Slot extraction: token-level F1 and span F1 (secondary)
- Hallucination rate: simple classifier + heuristics against ground truth (report as percentage)
- Latency p50/p95 and per-token cost estimate
- Quality regression alert: any drop > 2.5% absolute on intent accuracy or > 4% absolute on slot F1 triggers a regression flag and a follow-up triage.

Deliverables from Redwood
- Raw outputs (JSONL) + per-case diff with ground truth
- Aggregated metrics dashboard link + downloadable CSV
- Short summary with recommended model for pilot and config suggestions (batch size, quantization, cache policy)

Next steps (proposed)
1) You send the sample dataset and any high-priority prompt variations (we can accept a Dropbox/Drive link or S3).
2) We schedule a 30-min setup call with Neha (solutions engineer) to map dataset fields to our runner and provision access.
3) We run a 1–2 day evaluation and share results + recommended pilot config.

I've attached a runbook that includes the dataset schema and an example scoring script (redwood-eval-runbook.pdf). Looping in Neha (cc) to pick a setup time.

Thanks,

Hi Tom — answers inline and adding Neha to coordinate the technical setup.

1) Access & data handling- We can run the eval either in your VPC (recommended for regulated data) or in a private eval workspace in our hosted infra with strict retention settings. For VPC runs we provide an image and the orchestration steps; for hosted evals we default to 30-day retention for logs/outputs (can be shortened to 7 days upon request). We will not persist raw customer PII beyond the retention window and we can redact fields prior to ingestion if you prefer. I’ll have Neha follow up with our security playbook + SOC2 artifacts.

2) Estimated runtime / cost (3k rows)- Rough estimate: Redwood-3.1 quantized run ~ 45–90 minutes depending on batch config; cost estimate ~$400–$700. Redwood-1-7B run ~ 15–30 minutes; cost estimate ~$80–$150. Llama-family parity run depends on GPU type; estimate ~$200. These are ballpark numbers — we’ll provide an exact estimate once we confirm model sizes and batch settings.

3) Example scoring script snippet
We include a tiny Python snippet in the runbook, but here’s the core idea (pseudo):

# pseudo-code
# read example_dataset.jsonl -> for each case generate model_output -> compare intent_label -> compute accuracy and slot F1

from collections import Counter

def intent_accuracy(preds, gold):
    return sum(p==g for p,g in zip(preds,gold))/len(gold)

# slot F1 uses token/span matching; runbook includes implementation and unit tests.

I attached the runbook with the full script.

Practical next step: can you share a short anonymized sample (500–1k rows) so Neha can do a quick mapping and give a firm runtime/cost estimate? We can then schedule the 30-min setup early next week.

Thanks — Marissa
